name: How a self holds together
draftedBy: Claude, 15 Nov 2026, from Bryan's boundary, predict, act, aware framework in the Mind Atlas. The name, every line and the model's rules are a draft for Bryan to keep, change or strike.
why: A self is not a thing you have. It is an edge you keep up: between you and everything else, paid for with energy, and kept useful by guessing what comes next. See how that edge works and a lot of ordinary life makes sense, from a good week to a week when the world shrinks to the next hour.
outcomes: See a self as an edge that has to be paid for.
Say why what you can sense and plan for grows and shrinks with what you have to spend.
Tell a world that is short from a world that is unsteady, and what each one costs.
Say what a group gains and what it risks when its members share signals and food.

units.title: An edge that has to be paid for
units.outcome: See a self as an edge that costs energy to hold, and say what makes it grow or pull in.
units.needIt: How far ahead you can see and plan is not fixed. It grows and shrinks with what you have to spend, and with how well your guesses about the world hold up.
units.why: Every living thing, from one cell to a person to a town, keeps an inside apart from an outside. Keeping that edge up takes energy. What the edge lets it do is sense what is coming, guess where it will land, and meet it. When the guesses hold, more comes in than the edge costs, and it can afford to reach further. When they fail, or there is too little to go round, the edge pulls in.
units.reachesYou: A week with enough sleep and enough money, you can think about next year. A week with neither, you can only deal with what is in front of you. That is not a flaw in you. It is the edge being paid for with less.

lab.title: The edge
lab.ask: This is one small self. The dashed ring is how far out it can sense. Gold is food, pink is harm, and it has one gate to meet them with. Choose its world, guess what its edge will do, then watch.
lab.credit: A model of Bryan Korth's boundary, predict, act, aware loop. The reach is drawn after Michael Levin's idea of a cognitive light cone. It is a model to think with.

guess.ask: First, your guess. In this world, what will its reach do?

lab.triesNote: each strip is its reach over the whole run, all on one scale

rules.if: the world gives plenty and stays steady,
rules.then: its predictions land, more comes in than the edge costs, and its reach grows. A wider reach senses things sooner, which makes the next catch easier.
it cannot pay for a wide edge, so it pulls in. A smaller reach senses things later, with less time to turn, so it loses more of the little there is.

rules.if: the world gives plenty but is full of surprises,
rules.then: things swerve after it has predicted them. Each white flash is a prediction caught out, and each one is paid for. Put this strip beside your steady one: the same plenty buys a smaller reach.

rules.if: the world gives little and is full of surprises,
rules.then: it pulls in toward its body. Close in there is almost no time to predict, so what arrives is simply met or missed.

map: your boundary: how far out you can sense and care
the gap between your prediction and what happened
an action: you can meet one thing at a time
the energy that pays for all of it
lab.meet: Where you meet this: a week with enough sleep and money, when you can plan months ahead. A week with neither, when only the next hour is real. A job or a home where the rules keep changing, which wears you out even when nothing is short.
lab.draftedBy: Claude, 15 Nov 2026: a draft for Bryan to keep, change or strike.

units.do: Notice one day this week when your world felt small and only the next hour mattered. Ask what was short that day: sleep, money, time, or a world that kept changing on you.

units.title: Many small selves, one larger self
units.outcome: Say what changes, and what does not, when small selves join up.
units.needIt: Every group you belong to works this way: a body, a family, a crew, a town. Joining changes who gets warned, who gets fed, and who goes down when there is not enough.
units.why: Nothing new is added when small selves become a larger one. Each still pays for its own edge and makes its own predictions. What changes is the join between neighbours: what one senses, all know, and food flows from the fuller to the emptier. That is enough to keep alive a member that could never feed itself. It is also enough to tie every member to the same fate.
units.reachesYou: Your own body is this. Most of your cells never meet food; they are carried by the ones that do. So is a household with one income, and a team where one person hears the bad news first.

lab.title: Seven together
lab.ask: Seven small selves, each with its own reach, its own gate and its own energy. The one in the middle is walled in by the others and can never feed itself. Choose whether they are joined, guess how many will still be funded at the end, then watch.
lab.credit: The same loop as The edge, one scale up, from Bryan Korth's framework. The join follows Michael Levin's work on cells that share signals through gap junctions. It is a model to think with.

guess.ask: First, your guess. After a minute, how many of the seven will still be funded?

lab.triesNote: each strip is how many of the seven were funded, from start to end

rules.if: each is on its own and the world gives plenty,
rules.then: the outer ones do fine and the middle one stops. Nothing can reach it, and nobody passes it anything. Plenty all around it did not help.

rules.if: they are joined and the world gives plenty,
rules.then: all seven stay funded, the middle one too. It is carried by what flows in from its neighbours. Watch the joins light up: one senses, and all of them know.

rules.if: each is on its own and the world gives little,
rules.then: they stop one at a time. A few lucky ones are still going at the end, each for itself.

rules.if: they are joined and the world gives little,
rules.then: they share one fate. Run it a few times: most times either all of them make it or none do. Joining spreads what there is, so no one stops first, and when the whole is short it is short for everyone at once.

map: a join: signals and food pass along it
one sensed it, now all know
a member that cannot feed itself
its funding stopped, so it stopped
lab.meet: Where you meet this: a family that pools its money, where nobody goes without until everybody does. A crew where the lookout's shout turns everyone at once. The cells of your own body, nearly all of them fed by others.
lab.draftedBy: Claude, 19 Nov 2026: a draft for Bryan to keep, change or strike.

units.do: Pick one group you are part of. Ask what passes along its joins: who hears news first, and who is carried. Then ask what would happen to each of you if the joins were cut.

korth.name: Bryan Korth
korth.did: Worked out the boundary, predict, act, aware loop over years of his own notes, and built Void University.

levin.name: Michael Levin
levin.did: Showed that groups of cells use electrical signals to agree on what body to build and rebuild, and gave the name cognitive light cone to how far in space and time a living thing can pursue a goal.

friston.name: Karl Friston
friston.did: Proposed the free energy principle: that living things stay alive by keeping the gap between what they predict and what they sense small.
